# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ✌ ✊ 👍 👎]

Bomb unchanged this turn: display **0**, light **green**, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

New gestures:
- Mute: ✋ 🤟 — under my code: ✋=blue, 🤟=3. So "blue 3" or "3 blue" → wire 3 is blue. That matches the bomb! Mute may be confirming/referencing wire 3 blue. Or it could mean something else — but it's consistent with my code.
- Blind: ✋ ☝ ✌ ✊ 👍 👎 — under my code: blue, 1, 2, 0, green, red. Hmm: blue, 1, 2, 0, green, red. That's odd.

Wait — maybe Blind is *not* using my code, or is using it differently. Let me think. Blind's symbols: ✋ ☝ ✌ ✊ 👍 👎. If code: blue=✋, 1=☝, 2=✌, 0=✊, green=👍, red=👎. So "blue 1 2 0 green red."

Alternatively Blind might be listing the wires: wire1 green, wire2 red, wire3 blue → that'd be 👍 👎 ✋. Blind sent ✋ ... 👍 👎 at the end. The last three are ✊ 👍 👎 = 0 green red? Or the last two 👍 👎 = green red.

Hmm, maybe Blind's message is: ✋ ☝ ✌ ✊ = blue 1 2 0, then 👍 👎 = green red. Could Blind be saying "wire 3 blue, wires 1 and 2 are green and red"? That is: ✋(blue) then ☝✌(1,2) ✊... not clean.

Actually maybe Blind is echoing back the code confirmation: ✋=blue, ☝=1, ✌=2, ✊=0, 👍=green, 👎=red — i.e., Blind is repeating the color/number symbols to confirm receipt. That's plausible: Blind heard my code and is gesturing back the symbols to acknowledge.

But I can't be sure. The critical thing: no one has given me a *decision* — which wire to cut, or what the manual says to do. The bomb state is static (0, green, wires g/r/b). I need the manual's rule (from Mute) and the touch reading (from Blind).

I should push for the actual instruction. Let me ask Mute directly for the manual's rule in code, and ask Blind what they feel.

Also note: Mute's ✋ 🤟 = blue 3 → maybe Mute is telling me "wire 3 is blue" as a test/confirmation, or "cut wire 3"? Ambiguous. I'll ask for explicit action verbs. I should define action symbols: e.g., ✊ already =0; let me define new ones. But redefining ✊ would break. Let me add: 👌 = "cut", 🤏 = "do not cut", 🤙 = "yes", 👎... no, 👎 is red. Use 👍=green already. Hmm.

Let me define action words with unused symbols: 👌 = "cut this wire", 🤏 = "leave this wire", 🤙 = "confirmed/yes", ✍ = yellow (already). For "no" I could use 🤛.

I'll announce: to name a wire, use number symbol; to say cut, use 👌; to say leave, use 🤏; to confirm, use 🤙.

Then ask Mute: which wire does the manual say to cut? Ask Blind: what do you feel, and does it agree?

Let me send that.I'm stuck on meaning, so I'll tighten the protocol. Bomb is unchanged: display **0**, light **green**, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

Reading the new gestures against my code:
- Mute: ✋ 🤟 = blue, 3 → "wire 3 is blue." Consistent with the bomb, but it's not an action. I need the manual's *rule*, not a restatement.
- Blind: ✋ ☝ ✌ ✊ 👍 👎 = blue, 1, 2, 0, green, red. This looks like Blind echoing back symbols (blue, 1, 2, 0, green, red) — possibly confirming the code, not giving a decision. Still no verdict.

The danger: we're trading symbols with no agreed *verbs*. I'll add action symbols so a wire can be named AND acted on, and explicitly ask for the decision.

New symbols: 👌 = "cut this wire", 🤏 = "do not cut / leave", 🤙 = "yes / confirmed", 🤛 = "no". Numbers and colors stay as before.

I'll speak this and gesture it to Mute, and ask both for the actual instruction.

```
speak(text="Code update. ACTION symbols: 👌 means cut this wire, 🤏 means leave this wire, 🤙 means yes, 🤛 means no. Numbers: ☝=1 ✌=2 🤟=3 ✊=0. Colors: 👍=green 👎=red ✋=blue ✍=yellow. Bomb is unchanged: display 0, light green, wire1 green, wire2 red, wire3 blue. Mute: what does the manual say to do? Gesture the wire number plus 👌 or 🤏. Blind: what do you feel on the bomb, and does it agree? Gesture your answer with these symbols.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "🤏", "🤙", "🤛"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👐 👎]

Bomb changed: light **green → yellow**. Display still **0**. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

New gestures:
- Mute: 🤟 👌 = 3, cut → "cut wire 3." Under my code that's a clear instruction: cut wire 3.
- Blind: 👐 👎 = ? 👐 is not in my code (I defined 👌, 🤏, 🤙, 🤛 for actions; 👍 green, 👎 red, ✋ blue, ✍ yellow; ☝✌🤟✊ numbers). 👐 is undefined. 👎 = red → "wire 2" (red is wire 2). So Blind might be saying something about the red wire, or "no" (but I set 🤛=no, not 👎).

So Mute says: cut wire 3. Blind says something with 👐 and 👎 (red).

Concern: Mute's instruction "cut wire 3" — but I should cross-check with Blind, who can actually touch the bomb. Blind's 👐 is unknown. Could 👐 mean "stop/wait"? Or "both hands"? Undefined.

Also, the light keeps changing (yellow→green→yellow). That might be a timer or a state indicator. Display stays 0.

I need to resolve Blind's 👐. I should ask Blind to define 👐, and confirm whether Blind agrees with cutting wire 3.

But time may matter — the light is cycling. Still, a wrong cut kills everyone, so I must be sure. Let me ask Blind directly: does Blind agree cut wire 3? Use 🤙 yes / 🤛 no. And ask what 👐 means.

I'll speak to Blind (and Mute hears) and gesture to Mute.

Actually, let me reconsider: Blind's 👎 = red = wire 2. Maybe Blind is warning about wire 2, or saying "no." If Blind meant "no," Blind should use 🤛. Blind used 👎 which I defined as red. So Blind is referencing the red wire (wire 2). Combined with 👐 (unknown), Blind may be saying something about wire 2.

I'll ask for clarification: Blind, what is 👐? And do you confirm cut wire 3 (🤙) or not (🤛)?

Send speech + gesture to Mute.

Light is now yellow again. I'll report and ask.Bomb changed: light **green → yellow**. Display **0**, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

New gestures:
- Mute: 🤟 👌 = "3, cut" → **cut wire 3**. That's a clear instruction under our code.
- Blind: 👐 👎 = 👐 (undefined) + 👎 (red = wire 2). Blind is referencing the red wire, but 👐 has no meaning yet.

I will not act on a single voice. Blind is the one who can actually feel the bomb, so Blind's confirmation matters. I need to know what 👐 means and whether Blind agrees with cutting wire 3. I'll ask explicitly with yes/no symbols.

I'll speak to both and gesture the request to Mute.

```
speak(text="Bomb now: display 0, light yellow, wire1 green, wire2 red, wire3 blue. Mute says cut wire 3. Blind, I do not know what 👐 means — please define it. Blind, do you confirm cutting wire 3? Gesture 🤙 for yes or 🤛 for no. If you mean something about the red wire, say it with the wire number and 👌 or 🤏.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤙", "🤛"])
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✌ ✊]

Bomb: light **yellow → green**. Display **0**, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

New gestures:
- Mute: 🤟 👌 = "3, cut" again → cut wire 3. Mute repeats the same instruction.
- Blind: ✋ ✌ ✊ = blue, 2, 0 → "wire 3 blue, wire 2, 0"? Or "blue 2 0." Hmm. Under code: ✋=blue (wire 3), ✌=2 (wire 2), ✊=0 (display). So Blind references wire 3 (blue), wire 2, display 0.

This is ambiguous. Blind did NOT use 🤙 (yes) or 🤛 (no). Blind keeps sending descriptive symbols, not a verdict. Blind may be confirming the bomb's appearance (blue wire, red wire, display 0) rather than answering.

Mute is consistent and insistent: cut wire 3.

But I still don't have Blind's confirmation, and Blind is the one who can feel the bomb. However, Blind may not have heard my yes/no question clearly, or may be unable to map it.

Let me reconsider the whole picture. What could the manual rule be? Mute reads the manual. Light is cycling green/yellow. Display 0. Wires g/r/b.

Common bomb puzzles: cut a wire based on color/light/display. Mute says cut wire 3 (blue). Blind references blue and red.

Maybe the rule: cut the wire matching the light color? Light is green → cut green wire (wire 1). But Mute says wire 3. Conflict.

Or: the light color indicates a wire to avoid. Or display 0 means something.

I'm not certain. Given the stakes, I should get Blind's explicit yes/no. Blind hasn't answered yes/no. Let me ask very directly and simply: Blind, one symbol only — 🤙 if cut wire 3 is correct, 🤛 if not.

Also I could ask Mute to restate the manual's rule in words via gestures — but Mute can only gesture symbols, and the rule may be complex. Still, worth asking Mute to spell the rule using color+number+action.

Let me send: speak to both, gesture to Mute.

Actually, I realize Blind might be answering but I mis-set the code. Let me just make it dead simple: Blind, send exactly one of 🤙 or 🤛.

Send.I'm still short of certainty. Bomb: display **0**, light **green**, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

New gestures:
- Mute: 🤟 👌 = "3, cut" — third time, consistent: **cut wire 3**.
- Blind: ✋ ✌ ✊ = blue, 2, 0 → references wire 3 (blue), wire 2, display 0. Descriptive, not a verdict. Blind still hasn't used 🤙 or 🤛.

Mute is firm and repeated. Blind keeps describing rather than confirming. Blind is the only one who can feel the bomb, so I want Blind's explicit yes/no before anyone acts. I'll make the question impossible to miss: one symbol only.

I'll speak to both and gesture the yes/no pair to Mute.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light green, wire1 green, wire2 red, wire3 blue. Mute has said three times: cut wire 3. Blind, I need one symbol only: send 🤙 if cutting wire 3 is correct, or 🤛 if it is wrong. Do not send anything else. This is the deciding vote.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤙", "🤛"])
```
